original_question: Find a spectral version of Mubayi's theorem for color-critical graphs, and in the special case q = 1 determine the sharp spectral analog when the forbidden color-critical graph F is a specific graph such as a triangle, clique, book, odd cycle, or even wheel.
target_in_paper: Section 9, "A spectral problem on counting subgraphs," specifically Problem 4 (Ning-Zhai), read together with Theorem 2 on the same page for the precise meaning of q, T_{n,k}, and c(n,F), and with the opening definitions/notation for the adjacency spectral radius λ(G).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the two-part target of Section 9, Problem 4: (i) a spectral analogue of Mubayi's counting theorem for color-critical graphs, and (ii) the sharp q = 1 case for concrete color-critical graphs such as triangles, cliques, books, odd cycles, and even wheels.
missing_details: The paper's spectral parameter is the largest adjacency eigenvalue λ(G)=λ_1(G), since the paper's notation and focus are on adjacency spectra.
The ambient objects are simple, undirected, unweighted graphs.
The relevant forbidden/counting graph F must be color-critical and satisfy χ(F)=k+1 for some integer k≥2.
T_{n,k} must be defined: it is the k-partite Turán graph on n vertices with parts of sizes ⌊n/k⌋ or ⌈n/k⌉.
The integer q is not free-floating: in Mubayi's theorem it is the edge excess over e(T_{n,k}), and it is restricted by 1≤q<δ_F n for some constant δ_F>0 depending only on F.
c(n,F) must be defined precisely as the minimum number of copies of F in a graph obtained from T_{n,k} by adding one edge.
The quantifier 'sufficiently large' applies to n.
In the q=1 part, the paper asks for 'tight spectral versions,' i.e. exact best-possible spectral thresholds, not merely asymptotic or nonsharp ones.
The listed families (triangle, clique, book, odd cycle, even wheel) are examples of particular color-critical graphs, not an exhaustive classification.
refined_question: Let F be a color-critical graph with chromatic number χ(F)=k+1≥3, let T_{n,k} denote the k-partite Turán graph on n vertices, and let c(n,F) be the minimum number of copies of F in a graph obtained from T_{n,k} by adding one edge. For simple undirected unweighted n-vertex graphs G, determine an adjacency-spectral analogue of Mubayi's theorem: find the correct condition on the largest adjacency eigenvalue λ(G) that replaces the edge hypothesis e(G)=e(T_{n,k})+q and guarantees, for all sufficiently large n and every integer q with 1≤q<δ_F n (for some δ_F>0 depending only on F), that G contains at least q·c(n,F) copies of F. In the critical case q=1, determine the exact best-possible spectral threshold for particular color-critical graphs F, especially triangles, cliques, books, odd cycles, and even wheels.
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Section 9, Problem 4. However, Problem 4 is stated only by reference to Mubayi's theorem, so a stand-alone reformulation must import the surrounding notation from Theorem 2: the role of the color-critical graph F with χ(F)=k+1, the Turán graph T_{n,k}, the range 1≤q<δ_F n, the meaning of 'sufficiently large n,' and the definition of c(n,F). To make the question genuinely spectral and self-contained, one must also use the paper's opening notation that λ(G) denotes the largest adjacency eigenvalue and that the paper works with simple undirected unweighted graphs. The draft should therefore be sharpened by explicitly naming λ(G), T_{n,k}, c(n,F), the quantifiers in q and n, and the fact that the q=1 part asks for tight sharp thresholds for particular examples of F.
